texto:
May 1940. The British Army is trapped at Dunkirk, and Britain's Foreign Secretary wants to ask Mussolini what Hitler's terms might be.

The new Prime Minister, Winston Churchill, has been in the job for sixteen days.

For three days, the War Cabinet argues. Nine meetings. Churchill says the chances of decent terms are "a thousand to one against."

Then, as one minister recorded it in his diary, he tells his colleagues: let it end only when each one of us lies choking in his own blood upon the ground.

Years later, Churchill wrote that the question never even made the agenda. The minutes say otherwise.

The full story is on the channel. Before History Changed. Every story has a before.
